content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides a point UNDERDETERMINED using the wording of one passage/verse, which is what K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.","room":"When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open: (A) both meanings stand and the verse is not open; (B) the verse may still be UNDERDETERMINED because one phrase qualifies another.","why":"The judge text uses the single passage's two phrases (\"thy father\" and \"my Father's business\") to leave the point UNDERDETERMINED, while K-S2 says such a verse's two meanings both stand and the verse is not open."}
